requirement: Write a Money value object that normalizes amounts to cents with banker's rounding and currency codes to upper case, so equal values compare and hash alike, defers equality with foreign types, adds only matching currencies and has a round-tripping repr.
skeleton: Money class with __slots__, a validating and normalizing constructor, read-only amount and currency properties, __eq__ returning NotImplemented for foreign types, __hash__ over the same tuple, __add__ with a currency check, and __repr__.
caption: A money value object built from the decimal module. Money(amount, currency) strips and upper-cases the currency, raises ValueError saying bad currency code unless it is exactly three letters, and quantizes the Decimal amount to CENT with ROUND_HALF_EVEN, so equal values are stored identically. It uses __slots__ and exposes amount and currency through read-only properties. __eq__ returns NotImplemented when the other operand is not a Money, letting Python try the other operand's reflected __eq__, and otherwise compares the amount and currency tuple; __hash__ hashes the same tuple, so objects that compare equal hash equal and deduplicate in sets and dict keys. __add__ raises ValueError saying currency mismatch with both codes when currencies differ and otherwise returns a new Money. __repr__ shows the normalized amount and code. The fixture asserts that Money("10", "usd") equals and hashes like Money(Decimal("10.00"), " USD ") and deduplicates in a set and a dict, that 1.005 rounds to 1.00 and 1.015 to 1.02, that comparison with an object whose __eq__ always returns True is True while comparison with a string is not, that EUR amounts add, that USD plus EUR raises ValueError, that US, USDX, 12$ and an empty code raise ValueError, and the repr of 2.5 gbp.

plan.intent: Represent money safely as a hashable value
constraints: Equal amounts in the same currency compare and hash equal regardless of input form
Amounts are rounded to cents with banker's rounding
Comparison with a foreign type defers to that type
Currency codes must be three letters or ValueError is raised

rationale.teaches: Normalizing state in __init__ so __eq__ and __hash__ agree, returning NotImplemented from __eq__, and quantize with an explicit rounding mode.
rationale.why: An __eq__ without a matching __hash__ or a False instead of NotImplemented only misbehaves inside sets, dicts or mixed-type comparisons, and rounding mode differences only show on exact half cents.

ops.docstring: A money value object whose equality, hashing and arithmetic agree.

candidates.why_wrong: Hashing by identity gives equal values different hashes, so sets and dict keys keep duplicates.
Returning False for foreign types stops Python from trying the other operand's __eq__.
Currency codes keep their case, so usd and USD amounts never compare equal.
Rounding half up turns 1.005 into 1.01 instead of the banker's-rounded 1.00.
Adding amounts in different currencies silently produces a value in the left currency.
